spec.summary: Reads a pipe-delimited line containing principal amount, annual rate, and years count, validates each token as an unsigned decimal with digit-count limits, computes simple interest rounded to two decimals, and prints the result as a zero-filled 10-character number or an error message.

inputs.name: principal-amount
inputs.format: token 1, separated by '|'; human-readable number with literal decimal point where applicable; internal PIC 9(5)V99: unsigned number, 5 integer digits + 2 implied decimals (no decimal point stored), max 99999.99

inputs.name: annual-rate
inputs.format: token 2, separated by '|'; human-readable number with literal decimal point where applicable; internal PIC 9(3)V99: unsigned number, 3 integer digits + 2 implied decimals (no decimal point stored), max 999.99

inputs.name: years-count
inputs.format: token 3, separated by '|'; human-readable number with literal decimal point where applicable; internal PIC 99: unsigned number, 2 integer digits, max 99

outputs.name: printed-interest
outputs.format: PIC 9(7).99: display-edited, exactly 10 characters including explicit decimal point, zero-filled

outputs.name: interest-amount
outputs.format: PIC 9(7)V99: unsigned, 7 integer digits + 2 implied decimals, max 9999999.99

business_rules: The input line must contain exactly two pipe delimiters; otherwise display ERROR:INVALID_INPUT and stop.
Each token is validated by the Validate-Number paragraph before conversion: only digits and at most one literal period are allowed; a leading minus sign or any other character invalidates the token.
Whole-digit count must be at least 1 and not exceed the field maximum (principal 5, rate 3, years 2).
Fraction-digit count must not exceed the field maximum (principal 2, rate 2, years 0).
If a decimal point is present, at least one fraction digit must follow it.
After conversion, annual-rate must not exceed 100; otherwise display ERROR:INVALID_INPUT and stop.
Compute INTEREST-AMOUNT = PRINCIPAL-AMOUNT * ANNUAL-RATE * YEARS-COUNT / 100 with ROUNDED; intermediate decimals are exact and rounding occurs only when storing into INTEREST-AMOUNT.
On size error from the compute, display ERROR:OVERFLOW and stop.
Move INTEREST-AMOUNT to PRINTED-INTEREST (PIC 9(7).99) and display INTEREST= followed by the 10-character zero-filled edited value.
edge_cases: Input '100000.00|5.00|1' outputs ERROR:INVALID_INPUT because whole digits exceed the principal maximum of 5.
Input '100.00|100.01|1' outputs ERROR:INVALID_INPUT because annual-rate exceeds 100.
quirks: Validation rejects negative signs before NUMVAL is ever called; negative input is not reinterpreted as positive.
Leading zeros are allowed within each field's digit-count limits.
PIC 9 output is zero-filled; only Z suppresses zeros, and no Z edit characters are used.
The COMPUTE uses ROUNDED, so 1*12.35*(100-0.01)/100 = 12.348765 rounds to 12.35 when stored in PIC 9(5)V99; truncation occurs at the receiving field, not at each operator.
Each DISPLAY line is listed as one output item including all concatenated operands.

spec.summary: A COBOL program that reads a pipe-delimited line containing quantity, unit price, and discount percent, validates each token character-by-character, computes an exact total truncated to six decimals, checks for overflow, truncates to two decimals for the invoice total, and displays the formatted result or an error message.

inputs.name: quantity-count
inputs.format: token 1, separated by '|'; human-readable number with literal decimal point where applicable; internal PIC 9(3): unsigned number, 3 integer digits, max 999

inputs.name: unit-price
inputs.format: token 2, separated by '|'; human-readable number with literal decimal point where applicable; internal PIC 9(5)V99: unsigned number, 5 integer digits + 2 implied decimals (no decimal point stored), max 99999.99

inputs.name: discount-percent
inputs.format: token 3, separated by '|'; human-readable number with literal decimal point where applicable; internal PIC 9(3)V99: unsigned number, 3 integer digits + 2 implied decimals (no decimal point stored), max 999.99

outputs.name: printed-total
outputs.format: PIC 9(5).99, 8 characters wide with explicit decimal point and two decimal places

outputs.name: display-line
outputs.format: literal "TOTAL=" concatenated with printed-total, 14 characters wide

business_rules: The input line must contain exactly two pipe delimiters; otherwise ERROR:INVALID_INPUT is displayed and the program stops.
Each token is validated character-by-character: only digits and at most one decimal point are allowed; a leading sign such as '-' is rejected as 'when other'.

For quantity, whole-digits must be between 1 and 3 and fraction-digits must be 0; for price, whole-digits between 1 and 5 and fraction-digits between 0 and 2; for discount, whole-digits between 1 and 3 and fraction-digits between 0 and 2.
A decimal point with zero fraction-digits invalidates the token.
Tokens are converted with NUMVAL after validation; leading zeros are allowed within the digit-count limits.
Discount percent must not exceed 100; if it does, ERROR:INVALID_INPUT is displayed and the program stops.

The exact total is computed as quantity-count * unit-price * (100 - discount-percent) / 100 with intermediate decimal precision and truncated to six decimal places in EXACT-TOTAL (PIC 9(8)V9(6)) without ROUNDED.
If EXACT-TOTAL is greater than or equal to 100000, ERROR:OVERFLOW is displayed and the program stops.
EXACT-TOTAL is moved to INVOICE-TOTAL (PIC 9(5)V99), truncating beyond two decimal places without rounding.
INVOICE-TOTAL is moved to PRINTED-TOTAL (PIC 9(5).99), producing an 8-character edited output with leading zero fill and an explicit decimal point.
The final display line is "TOTAL=" followed immediately by the 8-character PRINTED-TOTAL.
edge_cases: Input "1|12.35|0.01" computes exact-total as 12.348765, moves to invoice-total as 12.34, and produces output "TOTAL=00012.34".
Input "999|99999.99|100.00" produces output "TOTAL=00000.00" because the discount factor is zero.
Input "-1|19.99|10.00" produces output "ERROR:INVALID_INPUT" because the minus sign fails character validation before NUMVAL.
Input "1|19.99|100.01" produces output "ERROR:INVALID_INPUT" because discount exceeds 100.
quirks: Validation counts digits before and after the decimal point but does not enforce a maximum token length beyond the PIC X(256) buffer.
A token consisting only of a decimal point is invalid because whole-digits is zero.
A token with a decimal point and no digits after it is invalid because fraction-digits is zero while dot-seen is one.
Multiple decimal points in a token are invalid.
The ACCEPT buffer capacity is 256 characters but is not a required line length; short lines are not padded.
UNSTRING splits the line on pipes into three 256-character fields without padding tokens.
COMPUTE truncates to six decimal places without ROUNDED; digits beyond six decimal places are discarded.
MOVE to PIC 9(5)V99 truncates beyond two decimal places without rounding; for example, 12.348765 becomes 12.34.
PIC 9 output fields are zero-filled; only PICTURE Z suppresses zeros.
There is no ON SIZE ERROR; results above field capacity silently lose high-order digits.

[static check, line 62] EXACT-TOTAL (PIC 9(8)V9(6): unsigned number, 8 integer digits + 6 implied decimals (no decimal point stored), max 99999999.999999) is stored WITHOUT ROUNDED: digits beyond 6 decimal place(s) are TRUNCATED, not rounded (e.g. 12.3333339 is stored as 12.333333, not 12.333334).

[static check, line 70] INVOICE-TOTAL (PIC 9(5)V99: unsigned number, 5 integer digits + 2 implied decimals (no decimal point stored), max 99999.99) is stored WITHOUT ROUNDED: digits beyond 2 decimal place(s) are TRUNCATED, not rounded (e.g. 12.339 is stored as 12.33, not 12.34).

spec.summary: A payroll calculator that reads hours worked and hourly rate from a pipe-delimited input, computes gross pay with overtime, applies progressive tax brackets, and outputs formatted pay amounts. Invalid inputs or overflow conditions produce error messages and terminate the program.

inputs.name: hours-worked
inputs.format: token 1, separated by '|'; human-readable number with literal decimal point where applicable; internal PIC 9(3)V99: unsigned number, 3 integer digits + 2 implied decimals (no decimal point stored), max 999.99

inputs.name: hourly-rate
inputs.format: token 2, separated by '|'; human-readable number with literal decimal point where applicable; internal PIC 9(3)V99: unsigned number, 3 integer digits + 2 implied decimals (no decimal point stored), max 999.99

outputs.name: printed-gross
outputs.format: PIC 9(7).99, 10 chars wide, display-edited with literal decimal point, leading zeros shown

outputs.name: printed-tax
outputs.format: PIC 9(7).99, 10 chars wide, display-edited with literal decimal point, leading zeros shown

outputs.name: printed-net
outputs.format: PIC 9(7).99, 10 chars wide, display-edited with literal decimal point, leading zeros shown

business_rules: Input must contain exactly one '|' delimiter; otherwise ERROR:INVALID_INPUT is displayed and program stops.

Both tokens are validated by validate-number: only digits 0-9 and at most one '.' are allowed; whole-digits must be 1-3; fraction-digits must be 0-2; if a dot is present, fraction-digits must be at least 1. If valid-input becomes 0, ERROR:INVALID_INPUT is displayed and program stops.
Hours worked and hourly rate are stored unsigned in PIC 9(3)V99 (3 integer digits + 2 implied decimals, max 999.99). Leading zeros are allowed within the digit-count limits.

Gross pay is computed with overtime: if hours-worked > 40, gross = (40 * hourly-rate) + ((hours-worked - 40) * hourly-rate * 1.5), rounded to 2 implied decimals; otherwise gross = hours-worked * hourly-rate. Intermediate decimals are computed exactly; rounding occurs once at the receiving field.

Tax is calculated on the rounded gross pay using progressive brackets: gross <= 500 => tax = gross * 0.10; gross <= 1000 => tax = 50 + (gross - 500) * 0.20; otherwise tax = 150 + (gross - 1000) * 0.30. Each tax computation is rounded to 2 implied decimals at the receiving field.
Net pay is computed as gross-pay - tax-amount.
Output displays 'GROSS=' + printed-gross + '|TAX=' + printed-tax + '|NET=' + printed-net as a single DISPLAY line.
COMPUTE ... ROUNDED rounds half away from zero at the receiving field; COMPUTE without ROUNDED truncates at the receiving field.
quirks: GROSS-PAY, TAX-AMOUNT, and NET-PAY are unsigned (PIC 9 without S); a negative intermediate result loses its sign and stores as the absolute value.

Without ON SIZE ERROR, a result too large for the receiving PIC field silently loses its high-order digits. This applies to GROSS-PAY (PIC 9(7)V99), TAX-AMOUNT (PIC 9(7)V99), and NET-PAY (PIC 9(7)V99).
Display-edited PIC 9(7).99 always outputs exactly 10 characters with a literal '.' before the last two digits; leading zeros are preserved.
The ACCEPT text buffer is capacity, not a required line length; short lines are not padded to 256 chars.
UNSTRING extracts tokens delimited by '|'; tokens are trimmed before validation.

validate-number rejects empty tokens, tokens with more than 3 whole digits, more than 2 fraction digits, a decimal point with no following digits, multiple decimal points, or any non-digit/non-dot character.
